text:
leila: hey folks, trying to finish my dev bootstrap on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04). Followed the handbook but running into two things: asdf nodejs install fails and brew can't talk to homebrew/core taps. anyone seen this?

john: welcome! paste errors?

leila: for brew: 
```
$ brew update
Error: Could not create /home/leila/.cache/Homebrew/Repository: Permission denied @ rb_sysopen - /home/leila/.cache/Homebrew/Repository/README
```

leila: and asdf/nodejs gives: 
```
Downloading node-v18.16.0-linux-x64.tar.xz...
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
```

diana: the brew permission error usually means your WSL distro was restored from a snapshot or you ran brew as root earlier. fix with `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.cache/Homebrew ~/.config/Homebrew` then re-run.

leila: that chown fixed brew update, thanks. asdf tar error persists though.

john: two possibilities: truncated download due to corp proxy, or missing `xz` / `tar` support. run `which xz` and `xz --version`?

leila: `xz` exists. I then tried `curl -L -o node.tar.xz <dist-url>` and it completes, but `tar -xf node.tar.xz` still errors: `tar: Unexpected EOF in archive`.

diana: that screams MITM/proxy replacing assets with an HTML error page. Are you behind the company proxy in WSL? Check `env | grep -i proxy`.

leila: env shows `http_proxy`/`https_proxy` set (from Docker Desktop integration). Removing them let me download the real tarball. How do others handle proxy + private registry?

john: we usually add the corp proxy to the distro but whitelist internal asset hosts. For binaries (node, go, rustup) we prefer bypassing proxy using `no_proxy` for `download.nodejs.org` and `static.rust-lang.org`. Example: `export NO_PROXY=download.nodejs.org,static.rust-lang.org,registry.redwood.internal` in `~/.profile`.

leila: nice. One more: asdf/nodejs plugin needs gpg keys; I get `gpg: keyserver receive failed: No route to host`.

diana: keyserver issues are common. We use the NodeSource keyring mirrors via hkps. Try: 
```
# install keys via curl
curl -fsSL https://keys.openpgp.org/vks/v1/by-fingerprint/9FD3B784BC1ABDD9 | gpg --import
```
Or enable `gpg` to use network through Docker Desktop by setting `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. If that fails, fall back to our helper which has pre-imported keyring: `curl -s https://s3.redwood/internal/bootstrap/nodejs-keyring.gpg | gpg --import` (requires okta).

leila: imported the keyring from the bucket (devops gave access). After that `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` worked.

leila: one last tiny gotcha for others: I needed `eval "$(direnv hook bash)"` and `export EDITOR=code` in `.bashrc` otherwise asdf prompts were blocked. Sharing in case new-hires hit similar.

infra-bot: INF-5022 created to track doc update: add proxy/no_proxy examples and a pointer to pre-imported keyring for WSL bootstraps (assigned: eng-infra).

leila: thanks all — all green now. happy to pair with anyone who needs a WSL walkthrough. :party:
